would-versus-will choice at a shared noun token
if-past versus when-present mood across two constructions
decision_changed: A recovering site adds mood to the corpus and its C, authored against canonical control v2, joins the comparable set directly. A capability stop would be the first failure for a function-word cue and would matter given that pronoun position, not cue type, is currently the best explanation of what fails.
novelty_delta: Twentieth behaviour. Prior-art search returns 0 events for modal, remoteness, would, will, conditional and subjunctive. The corpus has temporal frame (narrative_tense) but no MOOD variable: here an if-plus-past antecedent makes the consequent remote and obliges 'would', while a when-plus-present antecedent is factual and takes 'will'. The cue is a function word plus an inflection, spread across a subordinate clause, and the target is an auxiliary rather than a determiner, complementizer or preposition. Recipient and donor differ only in that antecedent and end on the same noun token; A2 embeds the whole conditional under a report frame.
